title: Mansi and Khanty
fact_summary: Two peoples of western Siberia whose languages are the closest relatives of Hungarian. Genetic studies use them as a reference for the conquerors' eastern ancestry.

claims.text: A study of the Uralic languages groups Khanty and Mansi together as Ob-Ugric, within Ugric.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: A 2019 genetic study found two paternal lineages among the conqueror elite, “both of which are present in Ugric speaking Khantys and Mansis”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: A 2022 study says the “immigrant core” of the conquering Hungarians “derived from an earlier admixture of Mansis, early Sarmatians, and descendants of late Xiongnus”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: A 2025 study finds “a low level of IBD connection” between the early medieval people of the southern Urals linked to the Hungarians and medieval groups on the river Ob, which it calls “possibly proto-Ob-Ugric”, “despite their close geographical proximity”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Living Mansi are a poor stand-in for the conquerors' ancestors; ancient groups from the Ural region are “much closer to the actual sources”.
claims.certainty_reason: A criticism of method made in one tier B study against the 2022 study cited above.

open_questions.text: Modern Mansi are used as a stand-in for ancient people. How much have the Mansi themselves changed in a thousand years?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.

contradictions.what_differs: Whether living Mansi are a fair reference for the conquerors' eastern ancestry. The 2022 study uses them; the 2025 study says older groups from the Urals fit better and finds few family ties between its Ural groups and the Ob region.
